messages:
maria: quick follow-up from the hosting abstraction RFC. i'm proposing a small pattern to keep hosted/dedicated/private from leaking assumptions: split the surface into a Capability Descriptor and a Runtime Contract. goals: explicit capabilities, a clear handshake, and a minimal test surface so implementations can be validated.
aj: ok curious. most friction ends up in auth, caching, and billing. how do you model those?
maria: short sketch pasted below — descriptor is declarative about features and constraints; contract is behavioral about execution guarantees. think of descriptor as the "what" and runtime_contract as the "how".

--descriptor example--
capability.identity = [token, mtls, platform-signed]
capability.kv_cache = prefetched | shared | none
capability.batching = continuous | fixed-ms-interval
capability.fallbacks = [model-variant, region, capacity-tier]
capability.network_requirements = none | intra-vpc | cross-region
capability.observability.min = [token_latency, kv_hit_rate, fallback_count]
capability.descriptor_version = v1

--runtime_contract example--
runtime.latency_slo_ms = 150
runtime.max_tokens = 4096
runtime.error_categories = [TRANSIENT, PERMANENT, AUTHZ, QUOTA]
runtime.eviction = least-recent-kv | tenant-affinity
runtime.rollout = optional { canary_percent, monitoring_hooks }

(we keep runtime.rollout optional so private installs can ignore it)

kevin: network_requirements is important. private installs should default to none and explicitly opt-in to shared cache modes. otherwise we silently require networking that air-gapped customers won't have.
sahil: +1. two other blindspots: 1) auth exchange mapping. hosted often injects a platform identity, private won't. we need a canonical translation layer in the handshake so callers get consistent identity semantics. 2) quotas/billing. dedicated wants commit semantics while hosted meters. descriptor should allow `quota.scope` and `quota.enforcement` so control-plane or runtime can enforce as appropriate.
maria: agreed. propose capability.identity include translation_hints and trust_boundary tags; and capability.quota.scope = token | route | tenant, capability.quota.enforcement = controlplane | runtime.
lucy: also add descriptor_version so older control planes can reject unknown descriptors. and standardize error categories — mapping to HTTP codes is an app concern but we need canonical categories in the contract.
aj: about caching: if kv_cache==shared we should require a `network_requirements=intra-vpc` and a minimal probe that validates kv warm-start. add a CI smoke job for that.

ops-bot: created CI template hosting-surface-smoke: runs auth handshake, kv warmup, fallback exercise. https://ci/internal/job/hosting-surface-smoke

kevin: observability: call out which telemetry is emitted by runtime vs control plane. add capability.observability.min array (token_latency, kv_hit_rate, fallback_count).
sahil: rollout mechanics: dedicated customers want canaries + automatic fallback. keep runtime.rollout but mark optional; platform can wire the hooks for hosted/dedicated. private can ignore.
maria: next steps: i'll draft an addendum to the RFC with the descriptor schema, handshake sequence (auth, descriptor validation, probe-first tests), and a test matrix covering auth, kv, batching, fallback, quotas, and rollout. sahil said he'll own the test matrix.
lucy: small test suggestion: include a compatibility test that sends an older descriptor_version and verifies the control plane rejects with a clear diagnostic.

kevin: one more operational note: when descriptor requests `network_requirements=intra-vpc` the deployer UI should surface a red flag for private installs. don't make this implicit.
maria: noted. i'll include UI/ops guidance in the addendum. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

aj: sounds good. please flag when draft is up and i'll eyeball the auth handshake diagram.
sahil: i'll start the test matrix doc today.

maria: draft will be posted Friday afternoon. if you see gaps call them out earlier.
